analysis: What changed versus the 6:00 AM brief: the tape reversed hard in the first 30 minutes of the regular session. Premarket futures had the Dow +0.7%, S&P +0.1% and Nasdaq-100 -0.8%; by about 9:55 AM ET the S&P was -1.40%, the Nasdaq-100 -3.22% and the Dow -0.44%, so Wednesday's rally is giving back across the board and the chip drag is no longer contained to futures. The selloff deepened after the open: AMD fell 12.2% despite a genuine Q3 beat (revenue $13.4B, +45%; data-center revenue $8.5B, +97%), which says the market is repricing the AI-capex cycle itself rather than trading the print. Micron fell another 10.2% on top of Wednesday's 7% drop, with the added weight of a paused $4.5B Taiwan plant, and Nvidia slid 4.8% to $190.52 ahead of its Nov 17 report. Tesla's 9.8% drop is the other big mover, extending Wednesday's political slide. The counterweight is macro, not stock-specific: Q3 productivity surged 3.6% versus 2.7% expected while unit labor costs fell 0.7%, a disinflationary read the tape is ignoring for now, and the Bank of England's first hike since August 2023 (25bp to 4.00%, 8-1 vote) adds a global tightening note. Apple is the lone megacap green (+0.9%), holding near its record. Signal vs noise: the broadening chip/AI-capex repricing, the Tesla slide and the productivity beat are signal; single-name earnings pops (AppLovin +33%) are noise for the index tape. No qualifying Hacker News or Reddit threads surfaced — the Reddit search returned nothing and the HN search returned no HN threads — so community_signals is empty rather than padded.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: The rally reversed in the first 30 minutes of the regular session: the S&P 500 fell 1.40% to SPY $755.96, the Nasdaq-100 fell 3.22% to QQQ $669.63 and the Dow fell 0.44% to DIA $530.69 (15-minute delayed, as of about 9:55 AM ET), unwinding part of Wednesday's gains (Dow +3.03%, S&P +1.58%, Nasdaq +1.44%).
headlines.why_it_matters: The premarket split is gone — the chip drag has spread to the whole tape, so the open is a broad give-back, not a rotation.

headlines.headline: Qualcomm fell 9.36% to about $156.98 in early trading (opened $150.06 vs a $173.19 prior close) after fiscal Q4 handset revenue fell 26% to $5.14 billion and chip-design margins were guided down to 20-22% from 24% on rising memory costs, despite revenue of $10.4 billion beating the $10.1 billion expected. At least eight brokerages cut price targets, including TD Cowen to $185 from $200 and Susquehanna to $165.
headlines.why_it_matters: The memory-cost margin squeeze is still the tape's main weight — Qualcomm's guide cut plus a wave of target cuts keeps semis leading the market down.

headlines.headline: AMD fell 12.15% to $429.38 in early trading despite reporting Q3 revenue of $13.4 billion (+45% year over year, vs about $13.1 billion expected) and record data-center revenue of $8.5 billion (+97%). It had closed Wednesday at $488.78, up 1%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A beat sold off double digits — the market is repricing the AI-capex cycle itself, not the quarter, which is a broader sentiment signal than any single print.

headlines.headline: Nvidia fell 4.80% to $190.52 in early trading (prior close $200.13) after falling 3.17% on Wednesday. It reports fiscal Q3 results on Tuesday, Nov 17, having guided this quarter's revenue to about $108 billion.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI leader is down less than the memory and handset names but still sliding into its Nov 17 report — the tape is de-risking the whole complex ahead of it.

headlines.headline: Micron fell 10.15% to $714.52 in early trading (prior close $795.23), on top of Wednesday's 7% drop to a three-month low. Micron also paused work on a planned $4.5 billion memory plant in Taiwan amid a labor dispute, per Bloomberg.
headlines.why_it_matters: Memory is the epicenter of the rout — a second straight day of double-digit percentage losses plus a halted plant expansion keeps the supply side in focus.

headlines.headline: Tesla fell 9.76% to $347.59 in early trading (prior close $385.19), extending Wednesday's 3.34% slide as Trump-aligned names keep falling after the Democratic midterm sweep.
headlines.why_it_matters: The political unwind is accelerating, not fading — Tesla is now down about 13% across the two sessions since the election result.

headlines.headline: Megacaps split in early trading: Apple rose 0.86% to $352.51, holding near its record, while Meta fell 2.91% to $611.65, Microsoft fell 1.60% to $546.93, Alphabet fell 0.66% to $287.02 and Amazon was nearly flat at $265.49 (-0.20%).
headlines.why_it_matters: Apple is the lone megacap green — the market is still treating it as a relative winner if data-center spending slows and memory prices ease.

headlines.headline: US nonfarm productivity surged 3.6% annualized in Q3, well above the 2.7% estimate, while unit labor costs fell 0.7% — a disinflationary tailwind for the Fed heading into Friday's payrolls.
headlines.why_it_matters: Strong productivity with falling labor costs eases the inflation worry, but the tape is ignoring the good macro print while chips dominate the session.

headlines.headline: The Bank of England raised rates 25 basis points to 4.00% in an 8-1 vote, its first hike since August 2023. Governor Andrew Bailey said another increase is likely if the US-Iran conflict continues, and the Bank sees UK inflation near 5% by mid-2027.
headlines.why_it_matters: A major central bank is hiking again on energy-driven inflation — a global tightening note that cuts against the lower-yields story that lifted Wednesday's rally.

headlines.headline: AppLovin rose about 33% to $360.17 in early trading after Q3 revenue jumped 55% year over year to $2.18 billion (vs $2.07 billion expected) and EPS of $4.30 beat the $4.03 consensus; it guided Q4 revenue to $2.365-2.395 billion (vs $2.25 billion expected) and added $3.2 billion to its buyback.
headlines.why_it_matters: The morning's clearest earnings counterweight — a genuine blowout with a raised guide — but it is a single name against a broad chip-led tape.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news today; the Nov 3 Q3 story carries forward: record revenue $357.2M (+43% year over year, vs ~$348.32M consensus), record Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF coverage 1.67x, EPS $0.33 vs $0.3345 expected, distribution held at $0.525, full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M. The $0.525 distribution pays tomorrow, Friday Nov 6. On the earnings call, management said over 60% of 2027 horsepower deliveries are contracted (about 90% of first-half deliveries), but flagged cost pressure: monthly lubricant costs exited Q3 about 25% above first-half levels and diesel hit an all-time high in September, with pricing not yet fully reflecting the increases.

watch_next: Friday Nov 6, 8:30 a.m. ET: October nonfarm payrolls (about 62,000 jobs expected, up from 29,000 in September; unemployment expected to hold at 4.2%); USAC's $0.525 distribution pays.
After the close today: Airbnb (EPS est. $2.85, revenue est. $4.75B), Cloudflare, Monster Beverage, Microchip Technology and IREN report Q3 results.
Whether the chip-led selloff spreads further into the broader tape or the Dow's relative resilience and the strong productivity print stabilize the session.
